newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares ends little changed in sleepy trade.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares ends little changed in sleepy trade.

text.p: ** (1015 GMT) Bombay blue chips finish mixed in lacklustre
trade after showing choppy movement this week
** Profit-taking pulls down market at start, but prices
consolidate in buying support seen at lower levels
** Bombay's top share index ends 5.36 points, or 0.12
** National Exchange index up 0.65 points at 1,215.55
** Aluminium major, Hindalco and State Bank of India buck
** India FII net inflows at $365.5 million in June against
Bombay's bull run brought the benchmark index to a 33-month high of 4,395.31 scaled earlier this week and in striking distance of an all-time high of 4,643.31 reached on September 12, 1994.
The recent stocks surge could catapult the index to new record levels, players said.
"Yes, it could very well. Fundamentally, of course that may not be the desirable level," Natwest's Sethi told Reuters.
"But, when it starts moving up, it would probably go there (4,643 level) and go past it."
